**Research question:** Is obesity a function of frequently eating high caloric foods?

**$H_0$:** Obesity is not a function of frequently eating high caloric foods.

**$H_1$:** Obesity is a function of frequently eating high caloric foods.

```{python}
# Imports and Data Ingestion
import pandas as pd
from scipy.stats import chi2_contingency
from IPython.display import display, Markdown
data = pd.read_csv("data/obesity_dataset.csv")
```

```{python}
# Re-map the Data and Verification
mapper = dict.fromkeys(["Obesity_Type_I", "Obesity_Type_II", "Obesity_Type_III"], "Obese")
mapper.update(dict.fromkeys(["Overweight_Level_I", "Overweight_Level_II","Normal_Weight", "Insufficient_Weight"], "Not Obese"))
data["isObese"] = data["NObeyesdad"].map(mapper)
assert data["isObese"].notna().all()
```

```{python}
# chi2_contingency Test
my_results = chi2_contingency(pd.crosstab(data["FAVC"], data["isObese"]))
mantissa, exponent = f"{my_results[1]:.3e}".split("e")
display(Markdown(f"$$\\text{{Result:}}\\quad "f"\\chi^2({my_results[2]}) = {my_results[0]:.2f}"f"\\qquad p = {mantissa} \\times 10^{{{int(exponent)}}}$$"))
```

Across $2{,}111$ records, about $51\%$ of those reporting frequent
consumption of high caloric foods were classified as obese, compared
with about $8\%$ of those not reporting frequent consumption.
Because $p < .001$ is below $\alpha = .05$, we reject $H_0$ and
conclude that obesity is a function of frequently eating high caloric foods.

::: {.callout-warning title="Partly synthetic data"}
Approximately $77\%$ of the records were generated using SMOTE;
$23\%$ were collected directly from users [@uci_obesity2019].
:::
